questions.q: Define verbal irony and situational irony in your own words, and give one example of each from *flYoj oSfMax* without quoting full dialogues — describe the scene and the ironic contrast.
questions.a: Verbal irony occurs when a speaker says the opposite of what they mean (e.g., ;'kksèkj ckcw mockingly calling fd'kunk "legkm baçkij" while actually resenting his worldly detachment). Situational irony occurs when the outcome contradicts expectations (e.g., ;'kksèkj ckcw spends his life rejecting fd'kunk's fatalism "tks gqvk gksxk", but in the end, he himself adopts that exact phrase as his only solace). A wrong answer that only defines the terms without textual examples reveals the student cannot connect abstract definitions to concrete textual moments — a fatal gap in board answers where evidence is mandatory.

Where my wife cooked. Where my children crawled." (2) Use the *house* as symbol of resistance — he locks himself in the upper room as bulldozers approach.
